# ADS: Architecture Description Standard

> A free, open-source standard that prescribes the structure, content, and quality criteria of Solution Architecture Documents (SADs). Built upon ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010, the 4+1 View Model, the cloud Well-Architected Frameworks, and TOGAF. Backed by a formal JSON Schema for machine validation.

ADS defines exactly which sections a SAD must contain, what each section must answer, and what "good" looks like at three documentation depths (Minimum / Recommended / Comprehensive — mapped to RFC 2119 SHALL / SHOULD / MAY). The current standard version is v1.3.2; the JSON Schema version is v1.0.0. The standard is published under CC BY 4.0 (content) and MIT (code) on the same repository.

Three names appear throughout. **ADS** is this standard. **SAD** (Solution Architecture Document) is the document you produce by following ADS. **HLD** (High Level Design) is the architectural-views and quality-attributes content that lives inside a SAD. So: ADS = the rules, SAD = the artefact, HLD = the design content.

The English version is normative. French and German translations cover orientation pages only (homepage, quickstart, cheat sheet, conformance and usage); the standard sections, examples, and templates remain in English by deliberate policy.

## Orientation

- [Overview](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/overview/): the structure, concepts, and rationale of ADS in one page; includes comparison with TOGAF, arc42, and cloud WAFs.
- [Quickstart](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/quickstart/): a 30-minute first-SAD walkthrough at Minimum depth.
- [Adoption Guide](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/adoption-guide/): how to roll ADS out in an organisation — evaluate fit, run a pilot, map to governance, customise, onboard architects, measure adoption.
- [Conformance and Usage](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/how-to-use/): conformance levels, depth model, RFC 2119 mapping, terminology table, compliance scoring.
- [Depth Cheat Sheet](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/cheat-sheet/): single-page table of which sections are required at each depth.
- [Design Principles](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/design-principles/): atomic fields, schema-as-truth, extensibility without ambiguity.
- [Framework Alignment](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/framework-alignment/): traceability to ISO 42010, 4+1, TOGAF, AWS/Azure WAF.

## The eight sections of a SAD

- [0. Document Control](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/0-document-control/): metadata, change history, contributors, sign-offs.
- [1. Executive Summary](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/1-executive-summary/): solution overview, business context and drivers, scope, criticality.
- [2. Stakeholders & Concerns](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/2-stakeholders/): register, concerns matrix, compliance and regulatory context.
- [3. Architectural Views (overview)](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-views-overview/): how the six views fit together.
  - [3.1 Logical View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-1-logical-view/): components, capabilities, design patterns.
  - [3.2 Integration & Data Flow](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-2-integration-view/): how components communicate internally and externally.
  - [3.3 Physical View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-3-physical-view/): hosting, compute, networks, environments.
  - [3.4 Data View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-4-data-view/): data stores, classification, data lifecycle.
  - [3.5 Security View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-5-security-view/): authentication, authorisation, encryption, monitoring, threat model.
  - [3.6 Scenarios](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-6-scenarios/): key use cases and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
- [4. Quality Attributes (overview)](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-quality-attributes-overview/): the five cross-cutting evaluation perspectives.
  - [4.1 Operational Excellence](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-1-operational-excellence/)
  - [4.2 Reliability & Resilience](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-2-reliability/)
  - [4.3 Performance Efficiency](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-3-performance/)
  - [4.4 Cost Optimisation](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-4-cost-optimisation/)
  - [4.5 Sustainability](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-5-sustainability/)
- [5. Lifecycle Management](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/5-lifecycle/): CI/CD, migration, test strategy, release, operations, decommissioning, exit planning.
- [6. Decision Making & Governance](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/6-decision-making/): RAID (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies), technical debt, guardrail exceptions, ADRs log, compliance traceability, sign-off.
- [7. Appendices](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/7-appendices/): glossary, references, supporting standards.

## Schema and templates

- [JSON Schema page](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/schema/): describes the schema's structure, with validation instructions in Node and Python.
- [JSON Schema (canonical URL)](https://archstandard.org/schema/v1.0.0/ads.schema.json): the machine-readable contract. JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Always validate against this URL.
- [Templates page](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/templates/): how to use templates, customise per-organisation, and convert between formats.
- [Markdown template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.md)
- [YAML template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.yaml)
- [JSON template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.json)
- [Word template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.docx)

## Worked example SADs

Seven examples, each available as a rendered page, raw JSON, and Markdown. All seven validate cleanly against the schema and exercise different industries, scales, and depths.

- [Examples index](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/)
- [Employee Directory](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/employee-directory/) — Minimum depth, internal HR app. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/employee-directory.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/employee-directory.md).
- [Customer API Platform](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/customer-api-platform/) — Recommended depth, regulated open-banking API. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/customer-api-platform.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/customer-api-platform.md).
- [Cloud Migration](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/cloud-migration/) — Recommended depth, lift-and-shift to AWS. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/cloud-migration.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/cloud-migration.md).
- [archstandard.org](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/archstandard-org/) — Minimum depth, the SAD for this very site. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/archstandard-org.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/archstandard-org.md).
- [NorthWind Retail](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/northwind-retail/) — Recommended depth, Tier 2, PCI-DSS regulated e-commerce on AWS. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/northwind-retail.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/northwind-retail.md).
- [Medwick Healthcare](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/medwick-healthcare/) — Comprehensive depth, Tier 1, fictional national-healthcare patient portal with FHIR R4 integration. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/medwick-healthcare.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/medwick-healthcare.md).
- [Stellar Platform](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/stellar-platform/) — Recommended depth, Tier 3, multi-cloud Internal Developer Platform on Kubernetes. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/stellar-platform.json), [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/stellar-platform.md).

## Guidance

- [What Good Looks Like](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/what-good-looks-like/): high-quality content excerpts.
- [Anti-Patterns](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/anti-patterns/): common mistakes with before-and-after examples.
- [Decision Guides](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/decision-guides/): flowcharts for picking depth, deciding when to threat-model, splitting SADs, capturing ADRs, classifying RAID items.
- [Reviewer Perspectives](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/reviewer-perspectives/): what an ARB chair, Security, Data, SRE, Finance, Change, and Product reviewers each look for.
- [Starter Kits](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/starter-kits/): pre-scoped guidance for new cloud apps, migrations, integrations, platforms.
- [Review Checklist](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/review-checklist/): printable one-pager for governance reviewers.
- [Industry Mappings](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/industry-mappings/): traceability to GDS Service Standard, NIST CSF, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, NHS DSPT, UK GDPR, FCA.
- [Cheat Cards](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/cheat-cards/): one-page printable references.
- [The 2-Minute Pitch](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/pitch/): speaker notes for introducing ADS internally.

## AI prompt library

Curated prompts for using LLMs against ADS. Each is published as raw Markdown ready to paste into ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or similar.

- [Prompts overview](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/prompts/): index of all prompts.
- [First-draft generator](https://archstandard.org/v1/prompts/first-draft.md): produce a structured SAD from a project brief.
- [SAD validator](https://archstandard.org/v1/prompts/validate-sad.md): completeness, consistency, clarity, credibility checks.
- [Compliance scorer](https://archstandard.org/v1/prompts/score-sad.md): apply the 0-5 compliance scale with justification.
- [Improvement suggestor](https://archstandard.org/v1/prompts/improve-sad.md): section-by-section suggestions for the next score level.
- [Security review](https://archstandard.org/v1/prompts/security-review.md): CISO-office-style review.
- [Governance review](https://archstandard.org/v1/prompts/governance-review.md): ARB-style review.

## Builder specification

- [SAD Builder Specification](https://github.com/andibing/archstandard/blob/main/docs/sad-builder-spec.md): defines what it means for a software tool to be ADS-conformant. Three conformance levels (Basic, Standard, Full). Use this if you are writing a tool that helps users author SADs.
